en: 1 Introduction
zh: 1　导论

en: There is a story in rural West Papua that tells of the cassowary,

, the founding spirit of the living world. At once creator, brother, father, and progeny, the cassowary brought forth humans, animals, and plants from a primordial mud, beaten and thrashed into form by the towering bird’s webbed feet over the span of a hundred thousand moons. It was the cassowary’s beak that nudged our knees and elbows into shape. It was the cassowary’s wattle that tickled our ears and noses into being. It was the cassowary’s feathers that slickened and smoothed our surfaces into skin. It was the cassowary’s grunt that tuned and tempered the pitch of what was later to become our voice. It is to the cassowary that we owe these traits – and it is to the cassowary that they return upon our passing.
zh: 西巴布亚乡间流传着一个关于食火鸡的故事。食火鸡称为khei，是生命世界的创始之灵。它既是创造者，也是兄弟、父亲与后代。在十万个月亮轮转的岁月里，这只高大的鸟用带蹼的双足反复踩踏、拍打原初的泥土，使之成形，由此创造了人类、动物与植物。是食火鸡的喙轻推塑出了我们的膝盖和手肘；是它的肉垂搔触出了我们的耳朵与鼻子；是它的羽毛把我们的身体表面抹得平滑，成为皮肤；是它低沉的鸣声调校、锤炼了后来成为我们嗓音的音调。我们这些特征都得自食火鸡；而当我们逝去时，它们也将归还食火鸡。

en: My first encounter with a cassowary took place along a dusty highway during long-term ethnographic fieldwork I was conducting among Indigenous Marind Peoples in the Indonesian-occupied region of West Papua – a place where the historical theft of sovereignty over lands, livelihoods, and bodies has, in recent years, been amplified by the proliferation of large-scale industrial oil palm plantations. I had, at the time, heard many stories from villagers about this mythical, revered, sacred, and mysterious being of solitary tendencies, whose presence is often known less through direct encounters than through the traces it leaves upon the landscape – deep footprints etched in the mud, sporadic rumbles overheard in the sago grove, wispy or wiry feathers caught on overhanging vines and lianas, and crushed berries strewn on the forest floor, bearing the characteristic dents of the bird’s powerful beak.
zh: 我第一次遇见食火鸡，是在一条尘土飞扬的公路旁。当时，我正在印度尼西亚占领下的西巴布亚地区，在马林德原住民族中开展长期民族志田野调查。在那里，土地、生计与身体的自主权历来遭受侵夺；近年来，大型工业化油棕种植园不断扩张，使这种侵夺愈发严重。彼时，我已听村民讲过许多关于食火鸡的故事：它富有神话色彩，受人敬重，神圣而神秘，喜欢独居。人们往往不是通过直接相遇，而是通过它留在景观中的痕迹感知它的存在：泥地上深深的足印，西谷椰林中偶然传来的低鸣，挂在垂枝与藤蔓上的轻柔或硬挺的羽毛，以及散落林地、留着它有力鸟喙特有凹痕的碎浆果。

en: But this cassowary was different. Noble and majestic it certainly was, with its sleek, iridescent plumage, and strong muscular legs. But it was also confused, distraught, terrified. The bird was standing in the middle of a dusty plantation road, caught by surprise as trucks, cars, and jeeps rushed past. It looked with panicked eyes to the licking flames of a burning forest on the left – one of many victims to the illegal land clearing through burning taking place at this time of the year. Then, it turned its gaze to the vegetal barricade of thorny oil palm trees on the right – a newly established plantation of over 50,000 hectares that now stood where a sacred sago grove had once flourished. Marinus, an Indigenous land rights activist and fellow traveller, turned to me and said, ‘See, the
’s fate is just like ours. The
has lost its home, it has no kin to flee to, its ancestors are turning into dust because of oil palm. The

inhabits a strange and dangerous place. Like us, it is confused and afraid. Like us, it is struggling to survive’. No sooner had my friend uttered these words than the cassowary dove with a desperate screech into the blazing forest, seemingly choosing flame over famine.
zh: 但这只食火鸡却不一样。它有光滑而泛着虹彩的羽毛和肌肉强健的双腿，的确高贵而威严；然而，它又困惑、慌乱、惊恐。它站在尘土飞扬的种植园道路中央，卡车、汽车与吉普车疾驰而过，让它猝不及防。它惊惶地望向左侧正在燃烧的森林，火舌舔舐着林木。这片森林，是一年中这个时节非法烧荒清地行为的众多受害者之一。随后，它又转眼看向右侧由带刺油棕组成的植物壁垒：一座新建的、面积超过五万公顷的种植园，占据了曾经繁茂的神圣西谷椰林。同行的原住民土地权利活动者马里努斯转头对我说：“你看，khei的命运和我们一样。它失去了家园，没有亲族可以投奔；因为油棕，它的祖先正在化为尘土。khei生活在一个陌生而危险的地方。它和我们一样，困惑而害怕；和我们一样，挣扎着活下去。”朋友话音未落，食火鸡就发出一声绝望的尖叫，扑进了熊熊燃烧的森林，仿佛宁愿选择烈焰，也不愿选择饥饿。

en: And so, I wondered in this moment: what kinds of justice can exist in a place where humans, non-humans, and ancestors find themselves caught in the colliding ecologies of forest and plantation? Who gets to story the lives and deaths of beings alternately sacrificed or starved at the pyre of agro-industrial capitalism, in all their unspeakable violence and vulnerability? What are the social and environmental consequences of a monocultural production system that is premised upon and perpetuates multispecies erasure and biocultural erosion? What possibilities might exist for more-than-human coexistence and collective future-building amidst the disfigured landscapes of the plantation zone?
zh: 于是，就在那一刻，我不禁追问：当人类、非人存在与祖先一同陷于森林和种植园相互冲撞的生态之中，这样的地方还能有何种正义？那些在农工业资本主义的火堆上时而被献祭、时而遭受饥饿的生命，承受着难以言说的暴力与脆弱性——谁有资格讲述它们的生与死？一种以多物种抹除与生物文化侵蚀为前提、又不断延续这两者的单一种植生产制度，会造成怎样的社会与环境后果？在种植园地带遭到毁损的景观中，超越人类的共存与共同建构未来，又可能以何种方式实现？

en: 1.1 Plantations as More-than-Human Landscapes
zh: 1.1　作为超越人类之景观的种植园

en: The plantation landscape described in this opening vignette constitutes one patch within what some environmental humanities scholars call the ‘Plantationocene’ – a spatiotemporal formation that entails ‘the devastating transformation of diverse kinds of human-tended farms, pastures, and forests into extractive and enclosed plantations, relying on slave labour and other forms of exploited, alienated, and usually spatially transported labour’ (Haraway 2015: 162). Today, monocultures cover some 80 per cent of the world’s arable land. As of 2019, oil palm plantations occupied 12 per cent of the land cover of Indonesia – the world’s top palm oil-producing country – and over 19 million hectares globally, with the figure quadrupling in the last fifty years (see Figure 1). Industrial soy – the fastest-growing cash crop in the world – now extends across 125 million hectares, with production doubling in the last twenty years. The proliferation of these and other so-called ‘flex crops’, like sugarcane and jatropha, has more recently been boosted by their promotion as sources of renewable biofuel, bioelectricity, and bioplastic, alongside food for humans and livestock. The international food, fuel, and finance crisis of 2008 has been a major accelerator of the large-scale acquisition and transformation of land for plantation developments across the Global South (Borras & Franco 2011).
zh: 开篇片段描绘的种植园景观，是一些环境人文学者所谓“种植园世”（Plantationocene）中的一个斑块。这一时空形态意味着：“把人类照料的多种农场、牧场与森林，破坏性地转化为攫取性的、封闭的种植园；它们依赖奴隶劳动，以及其他受到剥削、遭到异化、通常还被跨地域转移的劳动形式”（Haraway 2015: 162）。今天，单一种植约覆盖世界可耕地的80%。截至2019年，油棕种植园已占世界最大棕榈油生产国印度尼西亚国土面积的12%，全球面积则超过1900万公顷；过去五十年间，后者增至原来的四倍（见图1）。工业化大豆是世界上增长最快的经济作物，如今种植面积达到1.25亿公顷，过去二十年产量翻了一番。近些年，这些作物以及甘蔗、麻疯树等所谓“弹性作物”，除了供人类与牲畜食用，还被推广为可再生生物燃料、生物质电力和生物塑料的来源，推动了它们进一步扩张。2008年的国际粮食、燃料与金融危机，极大地加速了全球南方为发展种植园而进行的大规模土地获取和改造（Borras & Franco 2011）。

en: Monocrop plantations as such are emblematic of an era in which industrial activities are reconfiguring landscapes at a planetary scale in the name of profit, productivity, and progress. Within these monocultured spaces, variously described as ‘open-air factories’ (Lévi-Strauss 1961: 99) and exemplars of ‘military agriculture’ (Thompson 1975), visions of out-and-out exterminism and regimented homogeneity work hand in hand with dreams of endless growth. The consequences of these visions include damaged native ecosystems, soil degradation, freshwater depletion, chemical contamination, and exacerbated climate change and global warming resulting from rising greenhouse gas emissions. Plantations have also furthered the dispossession of Indigenous Peoples like the Marind of West Papua, as well as many other rural communities across the tropics, whose intimate and ancestral relations to land are routinely obscured, neglected, or violated by the state and corporate actors promoting and implementing monocrop developments (Chao 2022a, 2025). In both their human and ecological impacts, plantations as industrial infrastructures are indelibly tethered to longer histories of colonial expansion, capitalist incursion, territorial appropriation, corporate occupation, exploitative labour, and entrenched nature-culture divides that together legitimate the unsustainable extraction of natural resources and the subjection of marginalized humans to racialized hierarchies of worth (Koshy et al. 2022).
zh: 因此，单一种植园成为这样一个时代的象征：工业活动以利润、生产率与进步之名，在行星尺度上重塑景观。在这些被称为“露天工厂”（Lévi-Strauss 1961: 99）、也被视为“军事化农业”典范（Thompson 1975）的单一种植空间里，彻底灭绝的设想与严密规训下的同质化，与无限增长的梦想携手并进。由此造成的后果，包括本土生态系统受损、土壤退化、淡水枯竭、化学污染，以及温室气体排放增长所加剧的气候变化与全球变暖。种植园还进一步剥夺了西巴布亚马林德人等原住民族，以及热带地区许多其他乡村社群的土地。推动、实施单一种植开发的国家与企业行为者，往往遮蔽、忽视或侵犯这些社群与土地之间亲密而具有祖先传承的关系（Chao 2022a, 2025）。无论对人类还是对生态产生的影响，作为工业基础设施的种植园，都与殖民扩张、资本主义侵入、领土攫取、企业占据、劳动剥削，以及根深蒂固的自然—文化分野等更久远的历史不可分割。它们共同为不可持续的自然资源攫取提供正当性，并使边缘化人群受制于种族化的价值等级（Koshy et al. 2022）。

en: Aerial view of an oil palm plantation and adjacent road. Image credit: Pok Rie.
zh: 图1　油棕种植园及邻近道路的航拍图。图片来源：Pok Rie。

en: And yet, the rise and fall of plantations as ‘capitalist natures’ (Escobar 1999: 6, 11) have never been determined entirely by the humans and institutions who claim to create and control them. Nor are their forms and effects limited in substance and scope to the confines of monocrops as physical infrastructures, let alone distinguishable along rigid human-nonhuman divides. Rather, as this Element uncovers, plantations have always been and continue to be shaped by entangled processes of

extraction, extinction, and emergence. Extraction centres how commodities come into being through the harnessing of humans’ and plants’ bodies, labours, metabolisms, and affordances as exploited, uprooted, and often un(der)acknowledged workers. Extinction draws attention to more-than-human losses, erasures, and erosions of ways of being and relating as the by-products of industrial plantation production regimes. Emergence focuses on the new relations, institutions, and practices generated by monocrop systems, including those that challenge plantations’ technocapitalist, colonial, and racializing logic. This tripartite approach serves to structure the material that follows, but in a non-deterministic or mutually exclusive manner. For instance, extraction, extinction, and emergence can – and often do – occur simultaneously rather than sequentially. Similarly, what is experienced as extinction by one party might be apprehended as emergence by another. Human and other-than-human interests may align in certain instances, and at others diverge – at different moments, in different contexts, and to different ends. Importantly, the approach adopted in this work does not mark a shift away from the impacts of plantation logics on human communities – from questions of labour, political economy, and power, to realities of exploitation, violence, and vulnerability, among others. Rather, it invites a transformative expansion, pluralization, and cross-pollination of the ways in which these recurring motifs can be examined through an attention to their human
other-than-human manifestations, intersections, and frictions.
zh: 然而，种植园作为“资本主义自然”（Escobar 1999: 6, 11），其兴衰从未完全由那些自称创造并控制它们的人类与机构决定。种植园的形式与影响，其实质和范围也并不局限于单一种植的物质基础设施，更不能依照僵硬的人类—非人分界加以区分。相反，正如本书将揭示的，种植园始终由多物种的攫取、灭绝与涌现这些相互纠缠的过程塑造。“攫取”关注商品如何生成：作为受到剥削、被连根拔起、且常常不获承认或未获充分承认的劳动者，人类与植物的身体、劳动、新陈代谢及其可供利用的能力，被调动起来生产商品。“灭绝”使我们注意到，工业化种植园生产体制的副产品，是超越人类的存在方式与关联方式遭受丧失、抹除和侵蚀。“涌现”则关注单一种植体系生成的新关系、新制度与新实践，包括那些挑战种植园技术资本主义逻辑、殖民逻辑和种族化逻辑的关系、制度与实践。这一三分视角构成下文材料的组织框架，但它既不是决定论的，也不是相互排斥的。例如，攫取、灭绝与涌现可以——而且往往——同时发生，而非依次展开。同样，一方体验为灭绝的事物，另一方可能将其理解为涌现。在不同时间、不同情境中，为了不同目的，人类与非人存在的利益有时趋同，有时又相互背离。需要强调的是，本书采用这一视角，并不意味着将目光从种植园逻辑对人类社群的影响移开，无论是劳动、政治经济与权力的问题，还是剥削、暴力与脆弱性的现实。相反，它通过关注这些反复出现的主题在人类与非人领域中的表现、交汇和摩擦，促使我们的研究方式发生转变、得到扩展、趋于多元，并相互启发。

en: In approaching plantations as ‘human but not only’ (de la Cadena 2014), this Element thus reads against the grain of fictive yet enduring nature-culture binaries while pointing to the multifarious consequences of these divides for variously positioned human and other-than-human entities. It attends to how plantations make, unmake, and remake multispecies worlds as they enlist diverse protagonists in the production of new configurations of life and death, and of order and disorder. In doing so, the Element seeks to (re)tell plantation stories in ways that invite, provoke, reflect upon, and challenge assumptions of human exceptionalism, and that remain attentive to the complex intersections of race, coloniality, capitalism, and species animating plantations as ‘landscapes of empire’ (Besky 2013: 3).
zh: 因此，本书把种植园理解为“属于人类、却又不止于人类”（de la Cadena 2014），借此逆向审视那些虚构却长久存在的自然—文化二元对立，同时指出这些分野对处于不同位置的人类与非人实体所造成的多重后果。本书关注种植园如何召集各种参与者，生产生与死、秩序与失序的新构型，从而建构、拆解和重新建构多物种世界。通过这样的研究，本书试图以新的方式（重新）讲述种植园故事，邀请读者审视、激发其思考、反省并挑战人类例外论的预设，同时始终注意种族、殖民性、资本主义与物种之间的复杂交汇：正是这些交汇，赋予作为“帝国景观”的种植园以生命（Besky 2013: 3）。

en: 1.2 Positionalities and Audiences
zh: 1.2　研究者的位置与读者

en: I write this Element as an anthropologist and former human rights advocate who has conducted over a decade of ethnographic and investigative fieldwork in the Southeast Asian oil palm sector. Through my academic and activist career, I have sought to understand how Indigenous communities experience, theorize, and contest the adverse repercussions of plantation proliferation on their ways of knowing, being, and relating to human and non-human lifeforms. It is over the course of long-term, immersive participant-observation among Indigenous communities in the Indonesian-occupied region of West Papua that I became attuned to the multispecies dimensions of plantationscapes, which I grapple with from a trans-geographic and trans-temporal perspective in this Element. It is also this field-based research that has brought me to reflect on broader questions that haunt and heighten the ethical, political, and intellectual stakes of plantation studies. Who are the subjects of justice in plantation landscapes as more-than-human contact zones? What insights arise from thinking about plantation existence and counter-plantation resistance through a multispecies lens? In an age of ecological unmaking, what can plantation lifeworlds and afterlives teach us about the more-than-human dimensions of what Judith Butler (2004: 48) calls our ‘common corporeal vulnerability’?
zh: 我以人类学者及曾经的人权倡导者的身份撰写本书，此前已在东南亚油棕行业开展十余年的民族志与调查性田野工作。在学术与行动实践中，我一直试图理解：原住民社群如何体验、理论化并抗争种植园扩张所带来的不利影响，尤其是这些影响如何改变他们认识世界、存在于世，以及同人类与非人生命建立关系的方式。正是在印度尼西亚占领下的西巴布亚地区，在原住民社群中进行长期、沉浸式参与观察的过程中，我逐渐敏锐地意识到种植园景观的多物种维度；本书将从跨地域、跨时间的视角探讨这些维度。也正是这项田野研究，促使我思考更广泛的问题：这些问题始终萦绕着种植园研究，并使其伦理、政治与思想上的利害关系更加突出。作为超越人类的接触地带，种植园景观中的正义主体是谁？从多物种视角思考种植园中的生存与反种植园抵抗，可以获得哪些认识？在生态世界不断被拆解的时代，种植园的生活世界及其后续存续，能教给我们什么，使我们理解朱迪斯·巴特勒所谓“共同的身体脆弱性”（2004: 48）所具有的超越人类的维度？

en: In engaging with these questions, this Element responds to calls stemming from the environmental humanities to foster ways of knowing, engaging, and storytelling that recognize the significant lives of non-human others and enable us to cultivate other kinds of connections, accountabilities, and obligations towards the more-than-human world (van Dooren & Rose 2016: 77, 89). This approach articulates a ‘thicker notion of humanity’ that centres the embeddedness – rather than hyperseparation – of humans

multispecies communities (van Dooren & Rose 2012: 1; see also Plumwood 2002). It draws attention to ways of knowing more-than-human worlds that fall beyond the ambit of dominant, Western-rooted and secular scientific epistemologies, and that have been created, fashioned, and adapted to changing socio-ecological contexts by Indigenous Peoples, as well as by enslaved and otherwise exploited and marginalized communities.
zh: 通过探讨这些问题，本书回应环境人文学科的呼吁：发展能够承认非人他者生命之重要性的认识方式、参与方式与叙事方式，使我们得以同超越人类的世界培养其他形式的联系、责任与义务（van Dooren & Rose 2016: 77, 89）。这一视角表达了一种“更厚实的人性观”，把人类嵌入多物种共同体之中的状态——而非人类与之极端分离的状态——置于核心（van Dooren & Rose 2012: 1；另见Plumwood 2002）。它将目光引向那些超出占主导地位、植根西方的世俗科学认识论范围的认识方式：原住民族，以及受到奴役、剥削和边缘化的其他社群，创造并塑造了这些理解超越人类世界的方式，又使它们不断适应变化中的社会生态情境。

en: More specifically, this Element intervenes into environmental humanities debates on the origins and effects of the plantation form, which have seen renewed resurgence in recent years. Critical engagements with the concept of the ‘Plantationocene’ in particular have revitalized conversations across the social sciences, arts, and humanities on the relation between human and other-than-human violence and vulnerability within plantations (Davis et al. 2019; Jegathesan 2021; Chao, Wolford, Ofstehage et al. 2024). Transdisciplinary, multi-sited, and comparative approaches, such as the one adopted in this Element, are increasingly seen as necessary in understanding and analysing monocrop systems and societies (Forney, Rosin & Campbell 2018). Such comparative work, as I hope to demonstrate in the material that follows, helps uncover recurring motifs that have accompanied plantation proliferation globally, but also sheds vital light on plantations’ multiple and situated manifestations across space and time. It reveals how plantation imaginaries of simplification, scalability, and mastery over people, plants, and ecosystems in fact often operate alongside realities of plantation failure, patchiness, and contingency that belie their apparent homogeneity and timelessness. It uncovers how some plantations embody more explicitly than others the dynamics of extraction, extinction, and emergence – and how each plantation expresses these dynamics in its own particular way. It also invites us to reconsider all agro-industrial formations and legacies through their physical, ideological, and historical similarities and differences to those systems that are commonly labelled and recognized as ‘plantations’ per se.
zh: 更具体而言，本书介入环境人文领域关于种植园形式之起源与影响的讨论，这些讨论近年来重新兴盛起来。尤其是对“种植园世”概念的批判性探讨，使社会科学、艺术与人文学科重新展开对话，讨论种植园内人类与非人存在所承受的暴力及脆弱性之间的关系（Davis et al. 2019；Jegathesan 2021；Chao, Wolford, Ofstehage et al. 2024）。本书采用的超学科、多地点与比较性研究方法，日益被视为理解和分析单一种植体系及其社会所必需的方法（Forney, Rosin & Campbell 2018）。我希望通过下文说明：这样的比较研究，既有助于揭示全球种植园扩张中反复出现的主题，也能照亮种植园在不同时空中多样而具体的表现。它揭示出，种植园关于简化、可规模化，以及支配人类、植物与生态系统的想象，实际上往往与种植园失败、斑块化和偶然性的现实并存；这些现实否定了种植园表面上的同质性与超时间性。它也揭示，有些种植园比其他种植园更鲜明地体现了攫取、灭绝与涌现的动态，而每座种植园又以自身独特的方式表达这些动态。它还邀请我们重新思考一切农工业形态及其遗产，考察它们与通常被称为、也被认作“种植园”的体系之间，在物质、观念与历史层面上的异同。

en: On one plane, this Element is written for students and scholars in the environmental humanities and consonant disciplines, including anthropology, political ecology, multispecies studies, environmental history, geography, critical race studies, and science and technology studies. But it is equally of relevance to policymakers, non-governmental organizations, journalists, industry actors, and indeed, any member of the informed public who is interested in understanding plantations’ origins and forms and who is concerned or affected by plantations’ social and environmental impacts. On another plane, the Element speaks to all of us humans who inhabit this increasingly wounded and wretched place we call Earth (Gray & Sheikh 2018; Chao 2023). For wherever we happen to be rooted in the world, and no matter whether we have ever set foot in a monocrop, the foods and other resources that are produced through plantation systems are an intrinsic part of our everyday consumer lives. Raising awareness of our often invisibilized connections to, and complicities with, plantation violence is part of what this Element seeks to achieve, alongside identifying possibilities for creating less extractive relations to the plants, places, and peoples who fuel and feed us.
zh: 从一个层面说，本书面向环境人文及相关学科的学生和学者，包括人类学、政治生态学、多物种研究、环境史、地理学、批判种族研究，以及科学技术研究。但本书同样与政策制定者、非政府组织、记者、行业人士相关；实际上，也与所有希望了解种植园的起源与形式，并关注种植园社会及环境影响、或受到这些影响的公众相关。从另一个层面说，本书面向我们所有人：我们共同栖居在这个被称作地球、却日益伤痕累累和困苦不堪的地方（Gray & Sheikh 2018；Chao 2023）。因为，无论我们在世界何处扎根，也无论我们是否曾踏入单一种植园，经由种植园体系生产的食物及其他资源，都是日常消费生活不可分割的一部分。本书的一项目的，是让人们意识到我们与种植园暴力之间那些常被隐去的联系，以及我们对这种暴力的参与；同时也辨识出某些可能性，使我们得以同为我们提供燃料与食物的植物、地方和人群，建立较少攫取性的关系。

en: In the pages that follow, readers will travel diverse world-regions and time-periods through ethnographic and historical case studies that exemplify how plantations have been shaped by the agencies of both human and other-than-human protagonists – from indentured labourers, displaced communities, and environmental activists, to soils, parasites, and cash crops themselves. We will encounter, among many other bio-geographies, the colonial sugarcane, cotton, tobacco, hemp, and rubber estates of the Caribbean, United States, Hawai‘i, Brazil, Argentina, and Liberia. We will journey through contemporary oil palm, soy, tea, timber, and banana plantations in Indonesia, Cambodia, Italy, India, Paraguay, and the Philippines. We will consider these
fields through the lens of multiple

fields – from anthropology, critical race theory, geography, and history to political ecology, literary studies, agronomy, and plant biology. In the process, the diverse ways in which plantations are produced and experienced across space and time come to mirror the diverse ways in which they have been understood and addressed across disciplines.
zh: 在接下来的篇章中，读者将通过民族志和历史案例，穿行于不同地区与时代，了解种植园如何受到人类及非人参与者能动性的塑造：这些参与者既包括契约劳工、流离失所的社群与环境活动者，也包括土壤、寄生生物与经济作物本身。在众多生物地理场景中，我们将遇见加勒比地区、美国、夏威夷、巴西、阿根廷和利比里亚的殖民时代甘蔗、棉花、烟草、大麻与橡胶庄园；也将走进印度尼西亚、柬埔寨、意大利、印度、巴拉圭和菲律宾当代的油棕、大豆、茶叶、用材林与香蕉种植园。我们将从多个学术领域的视角审视这些实实在在的田地：从人类学、批判种族理论、地理学、历史学，到政治生态学、文学研究、农学与植物生物学。在这一过程中，种植园在不同时空被生产和体验的多种方式，与各学科理解和处理种植园的多种方式，将形成相互映照。

en: 1.3 Section Outline
zh: 1.3　章节安排

en: In Section 1, I consider how

in the plantation sector manifests in the coerced displacement of Indigenous Peoples from lands targeted for monocrop development under colonial regimes, in the uprooting and transplanting of enslaved and indentured workers from continents far removed from plantation geographies, and in the extraction of labour from the bodies of people subject to plantations’ racializing regimes. I also attend to how extraction shapes the worlds of cash crops as sources of metabolic work along with the worlds of so-called beneficial species whose biotic affordances are harnessed by corporations to sustain plantations’ ecological health under biological pest management programmes. In tandem, I reflect on instances where corporate-colonial systems of extraction fail, face resistance, or are otherwise threatened by the unexpected actions of human and non-human lifeforms – a topic I return to in further detail in Section 3.
zh: 在第1节中，我将考察种植园领域的攫取如何体现为以下过程：殖民体制强迫原住民族离开被划为单一种植开发对象的土地；把受奴役者与契约劳工从远离种植园的大洲连根拔起，移植到种植园；从受制于种植园种族化体制的人们身上攫取劳动。我也关注攫取如何塑造经济作物的世界——这些作物是代谢劳动的来源——以及所谓有益物种的世界：企业通过生物防治方案，利用这些物种的生物性能力来维持种植园的生态健康。与此同时，我将思考企业—殖民式攫取体系在何种情况下失败、遭遇抵抗，或受到人类与非人生命意外行动的其他威胁；这一主题会在第3节中得到更详细的讨论。
body.review: 原文此处及后两段称Section 1、2、3，对应的实际章节标题却依次编号为2 Extraction、3 Extinction、4 Emergence。译文保留原文编号；应按主题理解为三个主体部分，不据此改写目录编号。

en: In Section 2, I examine plantation lifeworlds and afterlives as drivers of multispecies

that are at once local and global, ecological and sociocultural. I trace the accelerating loss and critical endangerment of native flora and fauna that often accompany the substitution of biodiverse forests with industrial monocrops, situating this dynamic within a broader epoch of ecosystemic decline and planetary crisis. I uncover how the apparent homogeneity of monocrops masks realities of complex parasitic and mutualistic entanglements – some of which sustain cash crop yield and health, and others of which undermine it. I also consider the erosion of multispecies worlds and biocultural lifeways among communities whose lands are transformed into privatized plantations, reshaping in the process a range of more-than-human socialities, relationalities, and identities. I conclude by reflecting on the promise and perils of sustainability paradigms and conservation schemes that aim to offset the ecological harms caused by plantations, yet that often reinforce exclusion and dispossession through top-down approaches to environmental preservation and (neo)colonial framings of ‘nature’ as pristine wilderness.
zh: 在第2节中，我将考察种植园的生活世界及其后续存续，如何推动既是地方性的也是全球性的、既是生态性的也是社会文化性的多物种灭绝。我将追踪工业化单一种植取代生物多样性丰富的森林时，常常伴随出现的本土动植物加速消失、陷于极度濒危的过程，并将这一动态置于生态系统衰退与行星危机的更广阔时代背景之中。我会揭示，单一种植表面上的同质性，如何掩盖复杂寄生关系与互利关系相互纠缠的现实：其中一些关系维持经济作物的产量与健康，另一些却使之受损。我也将考察，当社群的土地转变为私有化种植园时，多物种世界及生物文化生活方式如何遭到侵蚀，进而重塑一系列超越人类的社会性、关系性与身份认同。最后，我将反思可持续性范式与保育计划的希望与危险：它们试图抵消种植园造成的生态伤害，却往往通过自上而下的环境保护方式，以及把“自然”界定为原始荒野的（新）殖民框架，进一步强化排斥与剥夺。

en: In Section 3, I turn my attention to modes of human and non-human being and becoming that find root in, yet meaningfully push against, the putative dominance and mastery of monocrop regimes over instrumentalized landscapes and lifeforms. I consider these modes of

in the context of plantations as laboratories for the production of colonial, postcolonial, and anti-colonial epistemologies of race, disease, and science, highlighting the frictions and cross-pollinations across different understandings of illness and practices of healing. I examine how plantations generate diverse meanings, moralities, and materialities through people’s engagements with cash crops, producing new vegetal-human intimacies while also shaping contemporary foodways and fuelling anti-colonial and anti-capitalist food sovereignty movements. I further consider how the racializing and ecocidal logics of plantations have given rise to new and counter-hegemonic identities, imaginaries, aspirations, and practices including art and aesthetics as politically charged sites of expression wherein plantations’ destructive yet contested effects are creatively represented, critiqued, resisted, and reimagined.
zh: 在第3节中，我将转向人类与非人的存在及生成方式：它们植根于单一种植体制，却又实质性地抵抗这一体制对工具化景观及生命形式所宣称的统治与支配。我将把种植园视为生产有关种族、疾病与科学的殖民、后殖民和反殖民认识论的实验室，在这一背景中考察上述涌现方式，着重讨论不同疾病理解与疗愈实践之间的摩擦和相互启发。我会考察，种植园如何通过人们同经济作物的交往，生成多样的意义、道德与物质性，生产新的人与植物的亲密关系，同时塑造当代饮食实践，推动反殖民、反资本主义的食物主权运动。我还将探讨，种植园的种族化与生态灭绝逻辑，如何催生新的、反霸权的身份认同、想象、愿望和实践。其中包括艺术与美学：作为充满政治意涵的表达场域，它们创造性地再现、批判、抵抗并重新想象种植园那些具有破坏性、又始终遭到抗争的影响。

en: In the Conclusion, I highlight the plurality of plantation systems and societies and foreground the urgency and challenge of attending to plantations through their concomitant inter- and intra-species dynamics. I consider the various ways in which plantation logics endure beyond physical agricultural fields and reflect on the promise of (counter)plantation futures and multispecies justice that might be unearthed in the troubled terrains of monocrop lifeworlds and their enduring afterlives.
zh: 在结论中，我将突出种植园体系及其社会的复数性，并强调：同时关注种植园相伴而生的种间与种内动态，既迫切，又富有挑战。我将考察种植园逻辑以何种多样方式延续到实际农田之外，并思考在单一种植生活世界及其持续不息的后续存续所构成的困顿地带中，可能发掘出怎样的（反）种植园未来与多物种正义。

en: 1.4 Terminology
zh: 1.4　术语说明

en: Finally – a few terminological clarifications. First, I intentionally refer in this Element to ‘plantations’ in the plural rather than to ‘plantation’ in the singular. I do this to underscore plantations’ situated and shapeshifting manifestations across space and time as recursive formations, rather than as homogeneous or monolithic systems in either existence or endurance (López 2011: 402; Thomas 2023: 354). Indeed, one of the key aims of this Element is to uncover how ultimately, and despite some prominent and recurring motifs, there is no such thing as ‘the’ plantation in any singular or static sense, but rather a
that varies across spatio-temporally defined contexts, practices, ideologies, communities, and the particular constellation of relations that connect and shape them.
zh: 最后，澄清几个术语。首先，本书有意使用复数形式“plantations”，而不是单数形式“plantation”。这是为了强调：种植园作为反复生成的形态，在不同时空中有其具体处境，并不断变形；它们无论在存在方式还是延续方式上，都不是同质或铁板一块的体系（López 2011: 402；Thomas 2023: 354）。事实上，本书的核心目标之一，就是揭示：尽管有些突出主题反复出现，但归根结底，并不存在任何单一或静止意义上的“那个”种植园；存在的是种植园多重体，它随着特定时空中的情境、实践、意识形态、社群，以及连接并塑造这些因素的特殊关系组合而变化。

en: Second, while I use the terms ‘plantations’ and ‘monocrops’ interchangeably within this Element, my primary focus lies more specifically with what Miles Kenney-Lazar and Noboru Ishikawa (2019: 63) term ‘mega-plantations’, or ‘plantation development that rapidly and radically transforms landscapes in ways that displace and replace preexisting human and nonhuman communities’ and that ‘require the application of large amounts of capital and political power and the transnational organization of labour, capital, and material’. Even within this definitional scope, I do not presume to cover plantation systems in all their taxonomic, temporal, social, economic, ecological or geographic diversity. To claim such a comprehensive and all-encompassing grasp on the myriad dimensions of plantation lifeworlds would be to problematically replicate assumptions of universalism and epistemic authority that are central to the ideology and operation of plantation logic itself.
zh: 其次，虽然本书交替使用“种植园”（plantations）与“单一种植”（monocrops），但我主要关注的，更具体地说，是迈尔斯·肯尼－拉扎尔与石川登所谓的“巨型种植园”（2019: 63）：即“迅速且彻底地改造景观，排挤并取代原有人类与非人社群的种植园开发”，而这种开发“需要投入大量资本与政治权力，并跨国组织劳动、资本及物资”。即使限定在这一定义范围内，我也不自称能够涵盖种植园体系在分类、时间、社会、经济、生态或地理上的全部多样性。若宣称自己能够对种植园生活世界纷繁的维度作全面而无所不包的把握，就会有问题地重演那种普遍主义与认识权威的预设；而这样的预设，恰恰居于种植园逻辑自身的意识形态与运作方式的核心。

en: Third, I use the term ‘multispecies’ in this Element to refer to lifeforms of all kinds, including plants, animals, and humans, but also elements, atmospheres, and landscapes that sustain human and non-human existence (Price & Chao 2022). This expansive definition makes space for abiotic entities that do not fit comfortably within Western secular scientific understandings or valuations of ‘life’, yet that have always been deemed sentient, animate, or otherwise agentive in many non-Western worldviews, including soils, waters, spirits, and the deceased (TallBear 2015; Chao 2026). It also positions humans within, rather than outside, the scope of ‘multispecies’, thereby allowing me to approach plantations as fertile – if fraught – grounds for engaging with the conjoined poetics and politics of race, culture, and nature (Moore, Pandian & Kosek 2003), as these shape and are shaped by, differential gradations, hierarchies, and categories of worth – within, across, and beyond species lines.
zh: 第三，本书使用“多物种”（multispecies）一词，指称各种生命形式，包括植物、动物与人类，也包括维系人类及非人存在的元素、大气与景观（Price & Chao 2022）。这一定义较为宽广，为非生物实体保留了位置：它们难以安置在西方世俗科学对“生命”的理解或估值之中，却在许多非西方世界观里始终被视为有感知、有活力，或以其他方式具有能动性；土壤、水、灵体与死者，都在其中（TallBear 2015；Chao 2026）。这一定义也把人类置于“多物种”的范围之内，而非之外，使我能够将种植园理解为一片肥沃——尽管充满张力——的土壤，用来探讨种族、文化与自然相互结合的诗学与政治（Moore, Pandian & Kosek 2003）：这些诗学与政治既塑造价值的不同层次、等级与类别，也被它们塑造，而这些区分既存在于物种内部，也跨越物种之间，并延伸到物种界线之外。
